articles.title: Bradley Beal Explains Wearing No. 3 Clippers Jersey After Chris Paul Retirement, 'No Disrespect'
articles.summary: Bradley Beal will wear No. 3 for the Los Angeles Clippers this season, but he was adamant he is showing no disrespect to his friend Chris Paul while doing so.
articles.body:
Bradley Beal will wear No. 3 for the Los Angeles Clippers this season, but he was adamant he is showing no disrespect to his friend Chris Paul while doing so.

"It's no disrespect to Chris. Chris and I are amazing friends," he told reporters Monday. "He's an amazing guy. Like I said before, his legacy is going to be up here [in the rafters]. What I'm doing ain't got nothing to do with that. … I'm happy to be wearing the number I've worn my entire career. I'm superstitious, didn't wear my number last year. I didn't play at all last year."

Beal also addressed the topic earlier this month when he said Paul's legacy with the Clippers "can't be touched, nor erased."

Paul wore No. 3 his entire career, including when he was with Los Angeles from 2011-12 through 2016-17 and again for his 16 games with the team last season before he was sent home in December.

He finished in the top seven of MVP voting five straight times during his first stint with the Clippers and led them to the playoffs in each of his six years.

The future Hall of Famer is also the franchise leader in assists, steals per game, assists per game and player efficiency rating, among other statistical markers, per Basketball Reference .

Notably, he revealed on 7PM in Brooklyn in February that Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank told him the team would retire his number:

For now, though, Beal will be wearing it as the three-time All-Star looks to bounce back from appearing in just six games during the 2025-26 campaign.

articles.title: LeBron James and the 76ers begin challenging quest for championship: 'Everybody's on the same page'
articles.summary: The process on making the 76ers work won't come overnight, but the goal is clear in Philadelphia.
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. — The gloomy, gray backdrop of the East Coast skyline, juxtaposed with the newest arrival from the West Coast, painted a poignant picture a few miles away from Philadelphia as the 76ers officially opened for business. Rain clouds hovered ominously around the facility, but, inside, the words emanating from LeBron James offered the security needed in stormy weather.

"Everybody's on the same page with the direction the organization, players, coaches and staff wants to be in," James said to reporters at Media Day on Monday, two months after shocking the NBA world by signing with the 76ers in free agency. "We all want to put the work in, that's most important. We're speaking the same language. That's exciting to be a part of."

There was a refreshing sense of authenticity and understanding from James as he outlined the reasoning behind his decision to take his talents to Philly. The pieces already in place — Tyrese Maxey , Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown — were a natural attraction but, at 41, after nearly a quarter century in the NBA, the opportunity to win (again) at a high level proved to be the tipping point.

But joining a new team with title aspirations comes with its side effects. LeBron is a gravitational force of his own, a draw unlike anything seen before in basketball for this current generation. His larger-than-life presence can diminish that of others or make for uncomfortable situations, something James not so subtly alluded to — which likely played a part in his decision to depart from the Los Angeles Lakers . But in discussions that ultimately led him to Philadelphia, James spoke in depth with Maxey about the other aspects that come with him and whether that could deter or detract from the rapid trajectory he was on. None of that seems to be an issue.

"I hope I have a similar mindset as him," Maxey said. "I believe in the work, he believes in the work. … Him being here is really cool. He's going to uplift the entire team. I'm focused on basketball, my job — the rest, I'm not really worried about. It doesn't bother me."

Having been to the Finals 10 times in his career (and amassed four Larry O'Briens), LeBron's obsession with winning another championship only makes this new partnership that much more interesting. The 76ers have notoriously tried — and failed — on numerous occasions to build contention-worthy groups, only to see them stumble for various reasons. Jimmy Butler . James Harden. Paul George . It's somewhat unfair to compare them to James' accomplishments and mileage, but the same goal of playing deep into May and June exists.

"I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round," James said sternly.

The process, no pun intended, on making the 76ers work won't come overnight, however. There will be growing pains. Outside of spot workouts here and there, this new-look group will take the floor for the very first time once training camp opens. Head coach Nick Nurse will be tasked with finding pairings that work, how to effectively share the ball between historically high-usage players and creating the trickle-down system that is suitable for all parties.

Still, there are areas where James' insertion will be felt almost instantly. Being swept in the second round at the hands of the eventual champion New York Knicks exposed the chasm that exists between the 76ers and true contenders, a difference made in part by a lack of mental advantage that the postseason beckons. If you subscribe to the notion that LeBron probably possesses the highest IQ of any player today, his in-game thought processes and how he sees the floor should be received with open arms.

"Just his approach," new (and former) teammate Kentavious Caldwell-Pope said. "When he shows up in the gym, he means business. He's gonna be locked in as far as whatever goals we've set as a team. He won't let anyone deter from that lane we're trying to keep everybody in. That's gonna be the biggest thing when we start."

The 76ers finished just 17th in points per possession and 23rd in half-court offensive efficiency last season, disappointing marks with that roster. With any system, there's a certain blend of talent, spacing and on-court IQ that generates shots. LeBron has historically been a positive in this aspect and his gravity — along with additions in Dean Wade (37.2% on catch-and-shoot 3s) and Anfernee Simons (45%) should assist in Philadelphia improving on their bottom-third ranks in made and attempted outside looks.

I'm somewhat concerned about how smoothly Brown's spacing pairs with James, given the former's inconsistency in off-ball scenarios — he shot less than 34% on catch-and-shoot opportunities last season — but given his all-around elite skill set, the 76ers don't necessarily need Brown to be a bonafide spotter. Ditto with Embiid, who hovers around 35%.

Reconfiguring the 76ers' playmaking structure shouldn't be that arduous of a task, either. Maxey once again stressed the desire to play more off the ball, which aligns well with how much LeBron likes the ball in his hands. James has a funny history with bad pass turnovers , a byproduct of having the ball in your hands that much, but Nurse will need to find the sweet spot between not overloading him with responsibility and keeping the other four players on the floor engaged playmaking-wise. Both Brown and Embiid are in the 93rd or better percentile in assist rate relative to their position, which should give Nurse optionality and creativity in his schematics.

(The reason why the onus will be put on the offensive end is because I expect slippage defensively. The 76ers finished as a slightly below average defensive unit and their summer additions, while tantalizing, don't scream defensive help. James will aid in their transitional stop rate, simply due to his smarts and physicality, but between Maxey, Brown and Embiid's unfortunate luck with injuries, the 76ers might be worn thin.)

Will this be enough to move this team into the upper echelon of title challengers? The overarching umbrella of how much LeBron has left in the tank will be the underlying theme for Philly this season. We're still talking about a player who grades out as a top-50ish talent , even at 41.

The financial commitment isn't substantial, the new depth makes it possible to lightly load manage him (along with Embiid) to keep him in shape for the postseason, and Nurse can stagger between Maxey and Brown in the meantime. Nobody who watched James dismantle Houston in the playoffs a few months ago (and kept the Lakers in games vs. Oklahoma City ) questioned whether the future Hall of Famer still has enough in his legs to go another marathon. But this next race, possibly his last, will be the most intriguing and challenging.

articles.title: 'That's Bulls--t,' Ben Simmons Calls Out Critics Who Say He Doesn't Love Basketball
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings forward Ben Simmons pushed back against the narrative that he doesn't love basketball during the team's media day on Monday, saying injury issues were the bigger reason he didn't play last season.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings forward Ben Simmons pushed back against the narrative that he doesn't love basketball during the team's media day on Monday, saying injury issues were the bigger reason he didn't play last season.

"I think that was more so my body. It wasn't about if I wanted to play. All these people talk about, I don't love the game. That's bulls--t," he told reporters (3:45 mark). "I love this game. If I didn't I wouldn't have taken that year to focus on myself and get back to where I'm at."

He also said basketball is "in my blood" and called it "my art."

Simmons, 30, didn't play last season and only appeared in 108 games between the 2021-22 and 2024-25 seasons, limited by a holdout during his final season with the Philadelphia 76ers and back issues .

The former Rookie of the Year and three-time All-Star won't be expected to play the ball-dominant and prominent role he once did in Philly. The Kings would assuredly be happy with him providing a defensive and playmaking spark off the bench as they build around a core group of De'Andre Hunter, Keegan Murray, Domantas Sabonis, Malik Monk, Darius Acuff Jr. and Nique Clifford.

Expectations are fairly muted about this Kings team in general, so Simmons will be making his return away from the spotlight that once burned very bright. Regardless, he isn't interested in anybody who questions his love for the game.

articles.title: Inspiring story on two careers, one vision: “We have an amazing team behind us that is taking the direction and the commitment"-How Stephen and Ayesha Curry built an empire while giving back to Oakland
articles.summary: Stephen Curry built his name by changing the way basketball is played.
articles.body: Stephen Curry built his name by changing the way basketball is played. Ayesha Curry built hers by turning her love for food, design and culture into a growing business world. Yet the story of the Currys goes beyond their individual success. Together, they have created businesses, produced entertainment and built a philanthropic organisation with a clear focus on Oakland. Even after the Golden State Warriors moved across the Bay, the couple continued investing in the community where they built their adult lives and started their family. Their journey shows how two very different careers can connect through a shared purpose.Stephen and Ayesha Curry built separate paths beyond basketballStephen Curry's career has never been limited to what happens during an NBA game. Alongside his work with the Golden State Warriors, he has developed a growing presence in entertainment and media through Unanimous Media, the company he founded with Erick Peyton in 2018.Unanimous Media has worked across film, television, publishing and podcasts. Its projects have included documentaries, scripted television and children's content, while Stephen has taken producer and executive producer roles across several productions. Ayesha has also worked with the company, serving as an executive producer on About Last Night, a celebrity couples game show created through a partnership between Unanimous Media, Fremantle and Sweet July.That shared space matters because Ayesha has developed a media career of her own. Her professional journey began with cooking and content creation before expanding into books, television, restaurants and entrepreneurship.Her Sweet July brand has become one of the clearest examples of that evolution. What started as a lifestyle magazine in 2019 grew into a broader company with a storefront, production and publishing operations, food offerings and skincare. By 2025, the Oakland-based business was using customer feedback to guide new product development, including an expansion into lip-care products.Ayesha's business story is important because it exists alongside Stephen's fame rather than simply beneath it. She has built a professional identity around her own interests, ideas and heritage.Ayesha Curry turned Sweet July into a growing businessAyesha's approach to business has been closely tied to authenticity. She has used food, family and her Jamaican heritage as foundations for Sweet July, while allowing the company to expand into new categories.In 2024, Inc. described Sweet July as a lifestyle, skincare, culinary, editorial and content production company. Ayesha explained that she sees herself as the person behind the big creative ideas while relying on her team to help turn those ideas into workable businesses.That approach has continued as the company has grown. In 2025, Ayesha explained that customer feedback had become a major part of Sweet July's product strategy. Rather than simply deciding what she wanted to launch, she began asking customers what they wanted to see next.The result is a brand that keeps moving without abandoning its original identity.Sweet July's connection to Oakland also gives Ayesha's business story another layer. The brand has promoted products from Black-owned and founded small businesses, creating space for other entrepreneurs alongside its own products.Meanwhile, Stephen's business interests have expanded in a different direction. His media company has built a catalogue covering sports, entertainment and storytelling, including projects connected to issues that matter to the Curry family.One example is SENTENCED, a documentary about childhood illiteracy. Stephen served as a producer and narrator, while Ayesha was also a producer. The project connected their entertainment work with a subject that would become central to their philanthropic efforts.Stephen and Ayesha Curry made Oakland part of their missionThe biggest link between Stephen and Ayesha's careers may be their commitment to Oakland.The Golden State Warriors left Oakland for San Francisco after the 2018-19 season, but the Currys stayed connected to the city. In 2019, they launched Eat. Learn. Play. with Oakland as its central focus. Their foundation's work covers three areas that reflect its name: nutrition, literacy and physical activity.Ayesha has explained why the city remains so important to them.“We just love Oakland,” Ayesha Curry said, standing next to her husband, in an interview with The Associated Press on Friday. “This is where we both became adults, where we started our life together, where we had our first child. And so for us, Oakland has always left this enormous impact on our spirits. And we’ve always said that we would continue to be a part of the community, even if we weren’t necessarily right in Oakland every single day.”That commitment has translated into a long-term programme rather than a series of one-off appearances.The foundation has supported school meals, literacy programmes, sports and schoolyard renovations. By September 2026, Eat. Learn. Play. reported that it had invested more than $100 million in Oakland students and families, provided more than 35 million meals, placed over 1 million books in students' hands, transformed 25 schoolyards and renovated six gyms.The numbers tell one part of the story. The other part is the way the Currys have tried to build a system around the needs of children.In 2024, they announced a $25 million, five-year commitment aimed at closing Oakland's literacy gap. The plan included high-impact tutoring opportunities for thousands of students.The Curry family is building a legacy beyond the NBAThe Currys' Oakland work has continued to evolve. In 2026, Stephen launched a scholarship partnership involving Davidson College, College Track and Oakland Unified School District. The programme is designed to give high-achieving students from underserved Bay Area communities access to Davidson through full scholarships.Their fundraising efforts have also grown. In August 2026, the Eat. Learn. Play. Workday Charity Classic raised more than $5.6 million. The foundation said the event helped push its wider Workday partnership close to $15 million.Another 2026 effort showed the scale of their network. A charity auction involving Warren Buffett, Stephen and Ayesha Curry raised a winning bid of $9,000,100, with Buffett agreeing to match the amount for GLIDE and Eat. Learn. Play.Stephen's community work was also recognised in July 2026, when he received the Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award for his impact through Eat. Learn. Play.Still, the most revealing part of their story may be that their individual careers have not disappeared inside their shared projects.Stephen remains a basketball star and an entrepreneur building a media portfolio. Ayesha continues to develop Sweet July and her work across food, lifestyle and entertainment. Their foundation gives those separate worlds a common destination.Stephen once described the meaning of their Oakland work in simple terms:“We have an amazing team behind us that is taking the direction and the commitment that Ayesha and I have to Oakland and leverage that to create amazing impact,” Stephen Curry said. “This is our 17th playspace renovation. And when you think back to our favorite moments, it is showing up, doing an unveiling, feeling the energy from kids, the teachers, administration. When they feel seen and they give you that energy back, it makes the world of difference.”That is what makes the Curry story larger than basketball or celebrity business. Stephen and Ayesha have built different professional identities, but they have found a way to make those identities work toward a shared goal. articles.title: LeBron James arrives as a 76er and sets expectations high: ‘I didn’t leave my family to lose in the second round’
articles.summary: In his first official duty as a 76er, James hit all the proper notes. He spoke graciously for nearly 20 minutes, and set expectations high for this coming season.
articles.body: A little after noon on a dreary Monday morning, kids wearing school uniforms spilled onto the playground in downtown Camden. It was recess at LEAP Academy, and the kids milled about the macadam or waited their turn on the swings, contentedly unaware that, just a few blocks away, the King had just arrived to claim his new kingdom. At around 11:15 a.m. ET, LeBron James followed a phalanx of front office and public relations staff into a second-floor room, sat down behind a table draped in blue cloth and promptly began clearing the table. He took a water bottle meant for his sipping and plopped it on the floor, yanked a microphone off its stand and finally glanced at a placard with his name. “You guys know who I am, right?” he said, before putting the name card on the floor, too. This, of course, is why James is here, wearing the red, white and blue of the Philadelphia 76ers: To rearrange things. To bring structure and order to a franchise that has been mired in mediocrity. And, if all goes as he plans, to upend the NBA pecking order. “I didn’t leave my family,” he said of his relocation to Philly while his family stays encamped out west, “to lose in the second round.” Had the Liberty Bell still been able, it might have peeled off in glee at that moment. In his first official duty as a 76er, James hit all the proper notes. He spoke graciously for nearly 20 minutes, waxing thoughtfully about the difficulty of juggling parenthood with superstardom, and sharing honestly his reasoning behind joining the Sixers. He invoked the Palestra (he played there as a high schooler) and paid proper homage to the demanding fan base (“We respect you, but we hate you. I love that,” he said). But it is those 11 words that Philly fans, who are at 25 years and counting without so much as a berth in the Eastern Conference Finals, will devour. The question, of course, is whether they will be on James’ statue or carved into his gravestone. Declarations here – of independence and otherwise – have a way of hanging around. The same people who embraced Moses Malone’s prediction of “Fo Fo Fo,” about the Sixers’ 1983 NBA title run (it wound up Fo, Fi, Fo) also remember that, 31 years ago, Ricky Watters replied, “For who? For what?” when asked why he didn’t lay out for a throw from quarterback Randall Cunningham. “They know sports. They know ball,” James said of his new fan base. “But if you’re not doing what you’re supposed to do, they’re going to let you hear it. They’re going to hold you accountable.” The worry about what will come, though, is for another day. For once, the September Sixers offered excitement about what could be. Ordinarily the Sixers’ media day would have fallen largely on deaf ears, a speed bump on a calendar filled with far more important dates. Nine hours after the Sixers commenced their interviews, the undefeated Eagles would play the Bears on “Monday Night Football.” On Tuesday, when training camp officially begins in Camden, the Phillies begin their quest for “Red October,” after belatedly securing a wildcard slot in the eleventh hour. But this Saturday, the Sixers will play their Blue x White scrimmage in the downtown arena for the first time, to allow for more fans, and the get-in price for the home opener is already pushing toward $300. Actual media day, usually reserved for a few ink-stained regulars, was near standing-room only, with one team official bemoaning a Phoebe Bridgers concert that prevented the team from moving the event to the team’s home arena in Philadelphia. This is what hope looks like, what it feels like when a franchise actually has a plan and not just a process. General manager Mike Gansey pulled off the coups of the offseason, not just signing James but securing Jaylen Brown in a trade with the Celtics that was as brazen as it was stealthy. “If it had leaked,” executive vice president for basketball operations Jameer Nelson told CNN Sports. “I’m not sure it happens. That’s just my opinion.” Brown’s arrival started the ball rolling. Tyrese Maxey sealed the deal. The precocious 25-year-old became a workout pal with James post-Covid 19 pandemic, the two bonding on their insatiable desire to do the work. In the offseasons since the pandemic, they became regular partners, both hitting 6 a.m. workouts together. Clearly impressed with Maxey’s dedication and pluck, James asked him for an honest evaluation of the Sixers. Still – even though Philly was on James’ agent’s famed whiteboard of destinations – it seemed like a long shot even to those involved. VJ Edgecombe was getting a pedicure when he heard about his new teammate and Nelson was at an AirBnB in Huntington Beach, California, for his daughter’s softball tournament when the news became official. Unable to tell his family, Nelson played dumb until Jayce started screaming, “LeBron is coming to Philly!” “Oh really?” Nelson said. Once the deal was done, Edgecombe set about creating a new team text chain. “But I don’t have LeBron’s number,” he said with a grin. “And even I did, I wasn’t adding him to it. I made Tyrese do that.” Even those on the text chain admit they’re still a little starry eyed. James officially became a Sixer on July 27, but this is his first time in Philly (that he arrived on the heels of a Nor’easter reminded him of what he’s in for with the East Coast weather). “I thought I was over it,” Jabari Walker said. “But then it was like, ‘Wait. He’s in the locker room now.’” On Tuesday, James will be on the practice court. That is, frankly, where he plans to do his best work. He can still play – “the luxury of my game is I can do everything,” he quipped. “Literally I can do everything” – but he thrives in creating an incubator for success. He threw shade at unnamed players who averaged big numbers in their careers, but secured no postseason success, and pooh-poohed an “instant oatmeal” society that wants everything handed out easily. James loves, at the risk of using a word that will make Philly fans flinch, “the process,” but his comes with four championship rings on his fingers. “You have to fall in love with doing things that are uncomfortable,” he said. “And if we can do that, we can be a great team. If we don’t do that, then we’ll be like, ‘Oh man. That was a great team on paper and we had a lot of great talent, and we lost in the second round.’”

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart extension talks create uncomfortable situation for Knicks title defense
articles.summary: The Knicks should be flying high in defense of their NBA title. Instead, they are facing questions about extensions, aprons and keeping the band together.
articles.body:
TARRYTOWN, N.Y. — Time and again on Monday morning, during a season-opening press conference at the New York Knicks ' practice facility, head coach Mike Brown emphasized how important it will be for his team to uphold the standard that led the team to the 2026 NBA championship.

As the Knicks open training camp and begin the process of defending their NBA title, Brown repeatedly said the team cannot afford any slippage — in their energy and focus, in their commitment to sacrifice and connectedness, in their willingness to hold one another accountable.

"First and foremost, we have to be able to look in the mirror and make sure that we're doing what we should be doing for everybody in the locker room — for ourselves and everybody else in that locker room," Brown said. "If we do that, the Knicks faithful will be taken care of, as long as we take care of ourselves first."

The biggest questions hanging over the Media Day session for a Knicks team seeking to defend a championship for the first time in 53 years, though, focused primarily on whether the team will take care of several of its core players, in the form of multi-year contract extensions.

Karl-Anthony Towns , the unicorn stretch-5 who played perhaps the best basketball of his life during New York's run to a title, has one fully guaranteed season left on his contract, and holds a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign. Josh Hart , whose boundless energy and hard-charging two-way work helped fuel the Knicks night after night, also has one fully guaranteed year left, plus a $22.4 million team option for 2027-28 .

Both are eligible for extensions of those contracts: up to four years and $272 million for Towns, and up to four years and $132 million for Hart. Both made clear Monday that they would very much like to secure those extensions, sooner rather than later.

"I mean, I've made it known," Towns said. "You know, I wanna play here. Been a fan since I was young, and so I would like to get one done, of course. That's obvious, you know? I would like to get it done so I can step on the court and feel [as] comfortable as possible."

"You always want to get it done, kind of as soon as possible, obviously, because you don't want that trickling into the season," Hart said. "Because whenever there's uncertainty, there's gonna be a lot of questions, there's gonna be a lot of rumors. At a human level, sometimes that can wear people down, and it can affect how you go out and handle business on a day-to-day basis, just some of that uncertainty."

Despite those desires, though, both starters enter training camp and the title defense without having inked long-term deals. Reports circulated last week that Towns and the Knicks were far apart on the terms of a new contract . And from the sound of Hart's comments on Monday, he's not particularly close, either.

"Do I think it's gonna get done [before the start of the season]? There hasn't really been much movement or conversation with that, so I don't think it will get done," Hart said. "But I would love for it to get done. Once the season starts, I'll probably have that mentality of, 'I don't really want to deal with this, I want to try and focus on playing the season.'"

All things being equal, you'd imagine the Knicks would prefer not to harsh the vibes of last year's triumph by heading into a new season with two of their five starters — plus key reserve Miles McBride , who's entering the final season of his bargain three-year, $13 million contract and is also eligible for a new deal — feeling ill at ease about their long-term standing within the organization. (McBride wasn't one of the players the Knicks made available Monday. He recently told Kristian Winfield of the New York Daily News that he's "a little disappointed" he doesn't yet have a deal done, but that he intends to be professional and perform while he waits.)

"I'm sure there will probably be a little extra weight to the jersey," Hart said. "You don't know the certainty of your situation and obviously it affects home life. There are certain things that you might want to do, but you're like, 'I can't, because I have no idea what the situation will be in two months, three months, four months, in a year, if I'm gonna be here or not.' You don't know. But hopefully, like I said, I'm a Knick. I'd love to be a Knick and I love the city."

All else isn't equal, though. The Knicks reportedly will not offer Towns or Hart the full boat, preferring instead to try to get both players to take something below their respective maximum salaries — as OG Anunoby and Jalen Brunson did in 2024, and as Mikal Bridges did in 2025 — to try to preserve as much financial flexibility as possible in the years ahead, especially with both Brunson and Anunoby eligible for extensions of their own next summer .

As much as Hart, Towns and McBride love the city — and as much as the city loves them for their contributions to last spring's magical run — the Knicks now find themselves facing down the same financial pressures that have helped induce owners and front offices to splinter championship teams across the league in recent years.

"That's why we haven't had a repeat [champion] for the last eight years," Hart said. "Because of that second apron and because of that [collective bargaining agreement]."

Four days after the Knicks finished off their five-game victory over the San Antonio Spurs , owner James L. Dolan went on New York radio station WFAN and made it clear that he did not intend to approve an offseason spending plan that would increase the team's total salary commitments for the 2026-27 season past $222 million — about $21 million above the projected luxury tax line , a threshold called the "second apron."

Dolan called the prospect of spending into the second apron something "that you'd have to be, you know, suicidal to do," since it not only imposes a higher tax rate on high-spending teams, but also strips away team-building and roster-management tools like access to salary-cap exceptions, the ability to aggregate players' salaries in trades, the option of sending cash to another team to grease the skids on a swap, and the freedom to acquire players in sign-and-trade deals, among other restrictions. Combine the financial penalties with the removal of roster-building tools, and the second apron becomes a very big, very scary boogeyman for teams intent on spending big to retain a championship-caliber roster. (A cynic might say it also becomes a very handy excuse/explanation for ownership groups looking to justify some amount of belt-tightening.)

Dolan's radio-appearance edict reportedly "blindsided" the Knicks front office, which wanted to go over the second apron after patiently and meticulously building a championship roster . Instead, New York spent its summer maneuvering to stay below that $222 million line — and, in the process, lost backup center Mitchell Robinson , who signed a three-year, $47.4 million deal with the Boston Celtics .

Watching Robinson, a critical reserve and the franchise's longest-tenured player, leave to join a rival for a deal that the Knicks restricted themselves from being able to offer or match, stung New York's starters.

"Yeah, definitely tough," superstar guard Jalen Brunson said. "That's my guy."

"I was heartbroken with that one, dawg," Hart said.

If the Knicks were committed to staying below the second apron, there was no way they were going to be able to afford Robinson. Even so, Towns said, his departure came as an unwelcome shock.

"I was very surprised," Towns said. "I was very surprised that Mitch wasn't gonna be back here with us. I think all of us were. It was a surprise to everybody. I thought something would get done there."

It didn't, so now Robinson plays in Boston, replaced by Andre Drummond , who will make about $12.5 million dollars less, helping the Knicks stay under the second apron this season. It's unclear whether Dolan's mandate to duck it will extend into the years ahead, too.

"If you asked me to give you three facts or two facts about the second aprons, I can't do it," Brown said. "I have no interest in that. I'm not trying to punt, but it is what it is. I don't follow that. [Team president] Leon [Rose] trusts me with the stuff on the court. And I trust him with that type of stuff. So whatever his thought is, or his focus is, I'm all on board with it."

In the absence of clarity on that organizational focus, though, it's natural for players without long-term security to start wondering about where they fit in. That seems like the kind of thing that could prove very distracting to a team trying to do something as difficult as repeating as an NBA champion. Brown said he invites his players to speak on the issues they might be dealing with rather than trying to brush them under the rug.

"You know, we try to talk about everything — we don't want to leave any elephants in the room," Brown said. "But you know, that's something that Leon and his group, they've been really good at, and some would argue be the best in the NBA at. And so I have a lot of faith in them and, you know, the players and the agents — whoever's involved, I'm not involved in it — that they'll figure it out. And our group has done a fantastic job of understanding that, you know, we can only control what we can control."

With the East still running through Madison Square Garden, even after a number of conference rivals reloaded this offseason, Brown wants Towns, Hart, McBride and all the rest of his players to be able to put business aside and focus on the task at hand on the floor. Brunson expressed confidence they'd be able to do so.

"Yeah, I feel like guys should be able to do that," Brunson said. "I think we're all professionals in that way."

At that point, though, the captain paused.

"I don't know. I guess we'll have to wait and see," he said. "See how we approach this. But I have the utmost faith in these guys — well, KAT, I don't know about Josh, we'll see how he acts. But we'll see."

Brunson's jokes aside, Hart — a veteran of nine NBA seasons and four separate trades — has been around long enough and seen enough to know that if things don't get done early, you can find yourself staring at the calendar, counting down the days and minutes until the trade deadline.

"We know that at the end of the day, it's a business," Hart said. "You have situations like that and you never know what's going to happen. But for me, as long as I wear this jersey, I'm gonna play as hard as I can for my guys and this city, and hopefully we can figure that out. But we know it's a business, and we know if some of these things aren't figured out by February, it might be a different conversation."

The glass-half-full take: Towns, Hart and McBride are all locked in for this season on a Knicks team that returns nine of its top-10 minutes-getters from the title squad, and should once again be excellent. The conversations on long-term deals can continue, too. SNY's Ian Begley reports that the Knicks have communicated they definitely want Towns and Hart around for the long haul; depending on the price points at which they can make that happen, perhaps there will be a pathway to bringing McBride back, too (though the math appears to be tight ).

"I would hope that that stuff gets done," Hart said. "At the end of the day, we're humans, and I think what sometimes gets lost is that we are people — that we all have lives and things that we have to deal with and fix. I wish I could sit there and say it wouldn't have any weight or any bearing, but you never know. Some people can handle it great and some people can really struggle with it and that can kill their performance. I hope it gets done, but we'll see."

And being forced into wait-and-see mode isn't fun — even while one of the things you're waiting for is your championship ring.

"I think in this situation, there is no comfortability to be had," Towns said. "So that's probably the best answer to that."

articles.title: Zion Williamson Lost 7 Pounds, In 'Impeccable' Shape After Injury History, Pelicans' Joe Dumars Says
articles.summary: Zion Williamson's injury issues and struggles at times with fitness have been prevailing storylines in a career defined by brief glimpses of transcendent talent but longer stints of unavailability.
articles.body:
Zion Williamson's injury issues and struggles at times with fitness have been prevailing storylines in a career defined by brief glimpses of transcendent talent but longer stints of unavailability.

But New Orleans Pelicans basketball operations chief Joe Dumars told reporters Monday at the team's media day that the star forward—who was listed at 277 pounds, seven pounds lighter than last season—is in "impeccable condition" ahead of the 2026-27 season.

"At some point, you just want the player to get it," he continued. "If someone has to call you every morning to drag you out of bed, to get you to work out, you don't get it yet. But when you're up and you're doing it, and you're the one leading it, then you start looking at that guy and you go, 'Okay, he's good.' ... That's what I saw from him this year. You can't play 82 games and not be in great shape. And so we talked about him being in impeccable condition and he has done that."

Williamson, 26, played 62 games last season, the second most he's played during a campaign in his career. He averaged 21 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.2 assists and a steal per game, shooting 60 percent from the field, though the Pelicans went just 26-56 and missed the playoffs for the third time in four years. New Orleans hasn't won a postseason series since the 2017-18 season and since being drafted in 2019, Williamson has missed 278 career games.

If New Orleans can stay healthy, a core of Williamson, Trey Murphy III, Dejounte Murray, Herbert Jones, Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears is interesting, though breaking into the playoffs in the West is no small task. But the team's upside begins and ends with Williamson.

articles.title: 'F--k No,' Dylan Harper Jokes About Winning Sixth Man Award, 'I Ain't Coming off No Bench'
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper was one of the best bench options in the NBA as a rookie last year, but he's looking to play a different role this year.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper was one of the best bench options in the NBA as a rookie last year, but he's looking to play a different role this year.

In an interview with GQ's Cam Wolf , Harper joked about winning Sixth Man of the Year before clarifying what he wants his role to be this year.

"What's the political answer here?" Harper said. "I'm going to do whatever the team needs me to do, man. If that's come off the bench…. That's crazy. F--k no. I ain't coming off no bench."

Harper, the No. 2 overall pick in 2025, put up 11.8 points, 3.9 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game last year, averaging 22.6 minutes per contest off the bench. He was tremendous in the Spurs' Finals run, recording 14.1 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, mostly off the bench in 23 games.

In his first career playoff start against the Oklahoma City Thunder, Harper posted 24 points, 11 rebounds, seven steals and six assists in a double-overtime win.

While Harper has proved that he's more than capable of taking on a starting role, the Spurs have a bit of a logjam in the backcourt. The typical starting lineup last season saw De'Aaron Fox at point guard and Stephon Castle at shooting guard, with Harper coming in off the bench.

Having three great guards is a champagne problem, and the Spurs will have to decide which of their three All-Star-caliber guards will have to come off the bench.

Harper clearly believes he'll be one of the two who get the starting nod.

articles.title: Pistons' Langdon Hasn't Spoken to Jalen Duren, Hints at Troubled Relationship with Zion Williamson
articles.summary: The biggest storyline for the Detroit Pistons this offseason has been the lack of a new contract for Jalen Duren, and the team's president of basketball operations, Trajan Langdon, gave some insight into how disconnected he has been with the young player.
articles.body:
The biggest storyline for the Detroit Pistons this offseason has been the lack of a new contract for Jalen Duren, and the team's president of basketball operations, Trajan Langdon, gave some insight into how disconnected he has been with the young player.

At Pistons media day on Monday, Langdon said that he and Duren, a restricted free agent, haven't spoken directly all summer, per The Athletic's Hunter Patterson . Langdon added, however, that he is looking forward to having Duren back on the roster, whether that is through him accepting the $9.6 million qualifying offer or signing a long-term deal.

While discussing Duren, Langdon alluded to his relationship with Zion Williamson when he was the general manager of the New Orleans Pelicans.

"I was in New Orleans for five years with a certain player that wasn't easy to deal with either," Langdon said. "We can control what we can control, and that's how we operate."

Patterson noted that Langdon was at the helm in New Orleans when the team included a weight clause in Williamson's 2022 extension. The Pistons' latest offer to Duren was a five-year, $200 million deal that included a weight clause, according to a report from The Athletic .

Duren has until Thursday to accept the qualifying offer from the Pistons, though Detroit can extend that deadline. ESPN's Shams Charania reported Monday that Duren will not attend the start of camp after rejecting the Pistons' latest offer.

Duren proved his worth with an All-NBA season last year, but a poor showing in the playoffs perhaps has Detroit wary of giving him the full five-year, $287 million deal he's eligible for.

With the season swiftly approaching, it wouldn't be surprising to see Duren settle for the qualifying offer and try his luck in unrestricted free agency next year.

articles.title: LeBron James ‘had visions’ of joining Knicks before they won championship
articles.summary: NEW YORK — LeBron James wanted to play for the Knicks — until they won a championship. James confirmed as much Monday, saying he “had visions” of finishing h...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — LeBron James wanted to play for the Knicks — until they won a championship.

James confirmed as much Monday, saying he "had visions" of finishing his career at Madison Square Garden before he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers over the summer.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player," James told ESPN during the Sixers' media day. "But after they beat San Antonio , I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James, 41, has gushed about the Garden throughout his soon-to-be-24-year NBA career, even though he's passed on multiple opportunities to sign with the Knicks, most famously in 2010.

Had the Knicks not won their first championship in 53 years in June, James could have made sense for them as a missing piece.

But the optics changed for James — a four-time NBA champion who has won titles with three different teams — once the Knicks ended their drought without needing his help.

"[The media] wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all," James said. "But much respect to the Knicks, obviously. An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out Jalen Brunson . I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at, and I'm looking forward to it."

Monday's confirmation came months after James' agent, Rich Paul, said on the "Game Over" podcast that the four-time NBA MVP would "be going to the Knicks" if they hadn't just beaten the San Antonio Spurs in the Finals.

At the time, James was still considering his free-agency options amid interest from numerous suitors.

James ultimately signed a well-below-market two-year, $8 million contract for a chance to compete for a championship with the star-studded Sixers, who also added Jaylen Brown this offseason to a returning core of Joel Embiid , Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe .

Still, James plans to live part-time in New York while playing his home games some 90 miles away, telling ESPN he will split time between "multiple residences."

James averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists per game last season with the Los Angeles Lakers .

The Garden wasn't as impressive to Spurs guard Stephon Castle , at least not in Game 3 of the Finals.

"It was underwhelming in that first game," Castle, 21, told GQ in a newly published feature. "They made it seem like it was going to be way crazier in there."

The circumstances for Game 3 — the Garden's first Finals game in 27 years — were unusual, considering President Donald Trump's attendance that night prompted heightened security and long lines to get in.

"OKC was way louder than MSG," added Castle, whose Spurs faced the Thunder in the Western Conference Finals.

The Garden atmosphere in Game 4 was much more raucous as the Knicks rallied back from a 29-point deficit and won, 105-104, on OG Anunoby 's go-ahead tip-in.

"That's the loudest I've ever heard an arena," Spurs guard Dylan Harper , 20, told GQ in that same feature.

After being fully cleared from offseason surgery, Brunson on Monday described playing through the injury in his left (shooting) wrist during the NBA Finals.

"It was painful, but I clearly could play through it," Brunson said Monday at the Knicks' media day in Tarrytown.

"Did what I had to do every single day, just to make sure I was right. Didn't think I necessarily needed surgery, so if that was the case, maybe I would have gotten it done sooner. But, yeah, I was just playing through it, didn't think anything of it, and I felt good."

Brunson won NBA Finals MVP after averaging 32.6 points per game — including 45 points in the clinching Game 5 — in the series.

Two days after he hosted "Saturday Night Live," Brunson hadn't decided on his favorite skit of the night.

"Ask me in like a week," Brunson said. "Because I still haven't really watched it, and I want to watch it."

Brunson became the first Knick and fifth NBA player to host NBC's long-running sketch comedy series.

Saturday's memorable moments included an opening monologue in which Knicks teammates asked Brunson questions from the crowd, as well as a parody of "High School Musical."

"I think his performance was fine," Josh Hart , who appeared in the monologue, deadpanned Monday. "I don't think he has a future in acting."

Karl-Anthony Towns came out of the offseason looking noticeably slimmer.

"My wife thought I looked good," the 7-foot center quipped.

More seriously, the 30-year-old Towns explained, "In the offseason, I always lose a lot of the weight. I put on the weight for the season. It's just good for my body, good for my knees. It keeps me young. I always use the offseason as a time to give my body a chance to recover, rest."
authors: Peter Sblendorio, New York Daily News

Dwight Howard and Amy Luciani might be working out their relationship following the NBA star filing for divorce for the second time.

The two sparked reconciliation rumors following Luciani's latest post on social media showed her documenting her vacation to Tokyo, Japan. In the Instagram post, the former reality star showed off her pink Chanel bag, herself lounging by the pool, a table filled with breakfast food, a skyline view of Tokyo, and more.

The NBA champion did not appear in the video or photos, but the comment section and Luciani's reaction implied that the couple might be trying to work things out.

What matters is that you both found your way back to each other, chose forgiveness, and chose your marriage. You don't owe the world perfection. articles.body: Bronny James makes a candid admission about what LeBron James leaving for Philadelphia means to him. The Lakers guard answered questions on Monday at media day in El Segundo. There was no complaint. Bronny reveals only a plain account of how the two handled it.Bronny heads into camp with a guaranteed $2.3 million contract, nine new teammates and a Christmas game against his father already on the calendar. He also has a clear idea of what he wants this season to prove. Together, they went on to achieve many NBA records, including creating history as the first active father-son duo to play and share the court together.Bronny James reveals how little he and LeBron discussed the Lakers exitBronny James took the question on Monday at Lakers media day, one day before training camp opened. LeBron James had left Los Angeles in free agency and signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, while his son stayed put. So how did the two talk it over?Not much, by Bronny's own account. He said the pair rarely go on business. Then he boiled the situation down to one line about careers, "He's got his own path, and I got my own." The 21-year-old guard added that LeBron knows he wants to make a name for himself and keep growing as a player.Bronny said he is happy for LeBron and curious to see how Philadelphia's season goes. He is also looking forward to the first meeting between the teams, on Christmas in Los Angeles. The Lakers are starting their first season without LeBron since 2017-18, and the roster around Bronny has changed a lot."I'm happy for him and excited to see where their season goes. I'm excited to see him on Christmas. I'm excited to play against him on Christmas, so that's going to be good," Bronny shared.He pointed out that LeBron is his real first name, and he said proving himself as Bronny is what gets him out of bed each day. The staff and his teammates are part of the curiosity too. "I'm excited for the experience, to experience something different," he told Spectrum SportsNet, according to Lake Show Life.Lakers star Luka Doncic felt the exit in his own way. He called it a little sad and said he learned plenty from playing beside LeBron.Bronny James is chasing a bigger role in year threeBronny spent the summer preparing to back up Doncic and Austin Reaves in the backcourt. He played 42 games last season and eight in the playoffs, and the $2.3 million guard carries a guaranteed deal into the new year.His best postseason night came in Game 4 against the Houston Rockets, a 115-96 loss. Bronny played a playoff career-high 15 minutes and finished with five points, two rebounds and four assists on 2-of-5 shooting. Los Angeles still won the series in five games.Bronny further admitted he is working on his decisions in frustrating moments, so coach JJ Redick has less reason to pull him."I'm coming in aggressive, playing smart, playing my game," Bronny said. He talks with Lakers newcomer Collin Sexton every day, hoping to borrow the veteran's drive on both ends of the floor. articles.title: Wembanyama y la obsesión de perder el anillo NBA: "He pasado noches sin dormir"
articles.standfirst: "Ganamos el Oeste el año pasado, no queremos hacer menos este año"
articles.summary: "Ganamos el Oeste el año pasado, no queremos hacer menos este año"
articles.body: El francés Victor Wembanyama aseguró que la derrota sufrida la pasada temporada en las Finales de la NBA es la mejor motivación posible para los San Antonio Spurs, que afrontan el nuevo curso con el objetivo de volver a pelear por el primer puesto de la Conferencia Oeste. "No podría imaginar una motivación mejor", afirmó Wembanyama durante la jornada de medios de los Spurs al ser preguntado por si la derrota en las Finales supone su principal motivación para esta temporada. El pívot francés, que afronta su cuarta temporada en la NBA, reconoció que todavía está procesando emocionalmente lo sucedido y admitió haber pasado momentos difíciles tras el final de la campaña. "He tenido algunas noches sin dormir, por supuesto. Quizá no noches sin dormir, pero a veces ha sido difícil conciliar el sueño, o he tenido emociones difíciles que a veces me persiguen", explicó. Wembanyama señaló que el equipo es consciente del largo camino que tiene por delante para volver a competir por el título. "Estamos en una gran situación. Tenemos mucha esperanza, somos muy ambiciosos y estamos preparados", declaró. Tras proclamarse campeones de la Conferencia Oeste la pasada temporada, el francés dejó claro que los Spurs quieren dar un paso más. "Ganamos el Oeste el año pasado, no queremos hacer menos este año. Queremos ser primeros y queremos seguir luchando por ese primer puesto", señaló. Wembanyama también destacó que la larga temporada mejoró su condición física y aseguró que llega al nuevo curso en mejor forma de la que esperaba pese al corto descanso veraniego. Además, valoró la incorporación del veterano Tobias Harris. "No tengo ninguna duda de que encajará perfectamente", dijo antes de destacar su experiencia y su capacidad para asumir un papel determinado y cumplirlo bien. El francés reconoció asimismo que la creciente atención que recibe puede resultar excesiva. "Sí, a menudo es demasiado. Pero está bien. Todo forma parte de esto", afirmó.

articles.title: "I had to wrestle my life back”: Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union opens up on how menopause changed her life
articles.summary: Dwyane Wade, the NBA legend, and his wife, popular actress Gabrielle Union, have remained pretty brave when it comes to speaking about their health and
articles.body: Dwyane Wade, the NBA legend, and his wife, popular actress Gabrielle Union, have remained pretty brave when it comes to speaking about their health and personal issues in public. While the Miami Heat legend Dwyane Wade has been public about his struggle and victory against cancer, Gabrielle Union has opened up about how her health issues affected her.Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union reflects on how menopause affected her and helped her to learn more about her healthA few months ago, in an interview with Eating Well, the popular actress Gabrielle Union reflected on how she takes care of her health post menopause as she said, “I had to wrestle my life back from my career. I realized I couldn’t keep burning myself out and skipping doctor’s appointments or annual checkups.”The “Being Mary Jane” actress added, “I’m a mom, a partner, a professional, but none of that works if I’m not healthy. Setting boundaries and saying no was hard, but I had to put my own health first. It’s like the oxygen mask analogy: you can’t help anyone else if you’re not okay yourself…I’ve realized that so many of the images we compare ourselves to, especially online, aren’t even real.”Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union also weighed in how menopause is a pretty different experience for each women as she said, “Every woman’s experience is different, and what works for one person may not work for another. Having open conversations with your healthcare provider is essential.”The popular actress added, “There are now FDA-approved, hormone-free options like Lynkuet® (elinzanetant) for women who may not be able to (or don’t want to) use hormone therapy. Knowing what’s available gives women the power to make informed decisions about their health.”Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union has been public and honest about her issues in lifeDwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union has been incredibly brave when it comes to speaking about all the issues she has faced in her life.For the unversed, Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union has been public about her assault when she was a young adult, about her struggle with fertility and some of the problems she has had with the three time NBA champion.When many actresses in Hollywood have preferred to keep their personal life away from the public life they live, Gabrielle Union has embraced it.Gabrielle Union has always spoken about her problems and has often inspired thousands of women across the world with her resilience and courage.While Gabrielle Union seems to be enjoying her life with Dwyane Wade and their daughter, she recently lost her father and has been dealing with his loss after he struggled with dementia in the last few years.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jordi Fernández, el jefe español en la NBA: "No vemos pasaportes, vemos grandes jugadores"
articles.standfirst: "Tenemos el tipo de plantilla en la que siento que todo el mundo puede jugar. Tenemos juventud y experiencia"
articles.summary: "Tenemos el tipo de plantilla en la que siento que todo el mundo puede jugar. Tenemos juventud y experiencia"
articles.body: El entrenador español de los Brooklyn Nets, Jordi Fernández, se mostró este lunes "extremadamente ilusionado" ante el inicio de la nueva temporada de la NBA, la liga profesional de baloncesto norteamericano, y aseguró que la competencia por los minutos será una de las claves de un equipo que combina juventud y experiencia. Durante la jornada de medios de los Nets, Fernández destacó el trabajo realizado por sus jugadores durante el verano y señaló que los jóvenes de la plantilla han ganado fortaleza y experiencia tras las últimas temporadas. "Tenemos el tipo de plantilla en la que siento que todo el mundo puede jugar. Tenemos juventud y experiencia", afirmó el ex seleccionador de Canadá, quien evitó anticipar quiénes formarán parte de la rotación. El técnico español insistió en que las oportunidades deberán ganarse con el rendimiento y la constancia y explicó que su responsabilidad será identificar a los jugadores que estén preparados para asumirlas. "Si eres así de bueno de forma consistente, no te preocupes, lo veré", señaló antes de añadir que su trabajo consiste en desafiar a cada jugador para que continúe mejorando. Fernández también defendió que el éxito colectivo debe estar por encima de los objetivos individuales: "Si nos centramos en el éxito del equipo, todo lo demás estará bien". El entrenador, cuyo contrato y los de todo su cuerpo técnico fueron renovados en abril, destacó además la importancia de mantener la continuidad del proyecto y aseguró que el objetivo es avanzar progresivamente. "Quieres mejorar un 1 %. No cinco, no diez, sino pequeños incrementos, siempre caminando hacia adelante", dijo. Sobre la creciente presencia de jugadores europeos e internacionales en la NBA, Fernández rechazó que el estilo actual favorezca especialmente a los europeos y consideró que refleja la globalización de la competición. "No vemos pasaportes en nuestro equipo. Vemos grandes jugadores con la posibilidad de desarrollarse", afirmó.

articles.summary: "Intento seguir creciendo. Lo más importante es hacer lo que te piden. Quiero ser un jugador ganador"
articles.body: El español Hugo González, alero de los Boston Celtics, aseguró que quiere seguir adquiriendo "ADN ganador" jugando en la histórica franquicia de Boston y destacó que su idea es prepararse como si tuviera que jugar "30 minutos cada noche". "Quiero seguir adquiriendo ADN ganador. Quiero seguir intentando hacer las cosas que nos hagan ganar. Quiero seguir haciendo las pequeñas cosas que pueden parecer pequeñas, pero que para nosotros no lo son", dijo González en el día de medios previo al arranque de la NBA. "Intento seguir creciendo. Lo más importante es hacer lo que te piden. Intento hacer lo que me piden y prepararme para todas las situaciones que se me presentan. Quiero ser un jugador ganador", explicó. "Tienes que estar preparado como si fueras a jugar 30 minutos cada noche, para que, si pasa, estés preparado", insistió el madrileño. González se prepara para su segundo año en la NBA, después de una primera temporada en la que ha destacado por su compromiso defensivo bajo las órdenes de un técnico Joe Mazzulla que le tiene alta estima. "El año pasado fue distinto porque la temporada europea es larga, pero tuvimos un gran verano, con mucho trabajo. Fui a España a entrenar y luego estuve en la Summer League; jugué mucho. Es algo que no debes dar por sentado. Pude seguir acumulando experiencias. Estuve dos semanas aquí y dos semanas en España. Pude tomarme una pausa para pasar tiempo con la familia y estoy ilusionado por comenzar", reflexionó. "Creo que sumar una experiencia en la NBA fue algo muy importante para mi carrera. Conseguí entrar en un entorno que me ha ayudado mucho. Estoy muy agradecido y eso solo me va a ayudar a ponerlo en práctica en mi segunda temporada. Espero poder seguir ayudando al equipo y, si puedo, mucho más", añadió en español.

articles.title: LeBron James admits he nearly joined the Knicks before Jalen Brunson won the NBA title without him
articles.summary: LeBron James revealed he nearly signed with the New York Knicks but backed off after Jalen Brunson led them to a title without him in free agency.
articles.body: LeBron James took the mic at 76ers Media Day, sounding like classic LeBron. After a summer of endless free agency rumors, opting out of his contract, and leaving his family on the West Coast to chase another ring in the East, he finally landed in Philadelphia. Yet before taking a single shot in a Sixers uniform, he was already laying down excuses and tossing his new teammates under the bus. "If we can do that, then we can be a great team," he said. "If we don't do that, then we'll be like, 'Oh man, it was a great team on paper. We had a lot of great talent, and we lost in the second round.' I don't wanna do that. I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round, I know that for sure. So the work needs to be done, and I'm ready to put the work in." Classic LeBron. If they win, he is the savior. If they lose, the team on paper simply did not put in the work. Then came the best part. LeBron admitted he nearly signed with the New York Knicks, but backed off after they won a championship without him, knowing fans would roast him online for pulling a Kevin Durant. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," LeBron said. "One of the best places I've ever played. I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it. Y'all wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all." "But much respect to the Knicks, obviously," LeBron added. "An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out Jalen Brunson. I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at, and I'm looking forward to it." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He wanted to end the drought himself. Once Jalen Brunson took care of business, LeBron bailed for Philly. Dropping LeBron into that locker room immediately raised questions about who actually runs the show in Philadelphia. Asked on Monday who the "alpha" of the Sixers is, Jaylen Brown shut it down cold: "Next question." "And if you're not doing what you're supposed to do, they're going to let you hear it, and I'm excited about that." Sure you are, LeBron. As for how he fits alongside Embiid and Tyrese Maxey entering Season 24, LeBron had zero doubts about his remaining capability. "The luxury of my game is that I can do everything," James declared. "Literally, I can do everything." "I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team, and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey ..." articles.title: Enemigos íntimos: el Barça visita a Xavi Pascual y el Real Madrid, a Laso
articles.standfirst: Los dos grandes se enfrentan a los técnicos que marcaron su historia reciente: 30 títulos entre los dos
articles.summary: Los dos grandes se enfrentan a los técnicos que marcaron su historia reciente: 30 títulos entre los dos
articles.body: En ocasiones, el calendario de las competiciones es caprichoso. Por ejemplo, en esta segunda jornada de la Euroliga, que también es el inicio de la primera doble que habrá esta temporada. El Barça y el Real Madrid afrontan partidos a domicilio en los que se van a enfrentar a parte de su pasado reciente. Uno, además, muy brillante. Los azulgranas visitan al Dubai Basketball dirigido por Xavi Pascual (18.00 horas) y los blancos juegan en Estambul ante el Anadolu Efes de Pablo Laso (19.00 h.). Pascual lideró una gran era del Barça, del que se hizo cargo en 2008 y salió en 2016. En ese tiempo ganó una Euroliga, cuatro ACB y tres Copas. Este verano cerró su segunda etapa como entrenador culé y no fue ni por asomo tan exitosa como la anterior. Había comenzado en febrero, cuando cogió un equipo desnortado. Sin embargo, las promesas incumplidas de la directiva hicieron que, cuando llegó la oferta de Dubai, decidiera pagar su cláusula e irse. El técnico catalán ya se midió al Barça cuando dirigía al Panathinaikos y al Zenit, pero ahora será especial por lo frescos que están los acontecimientos. “Tratamos este partido de la misma manera que todos. Me voy a encontrar con mucha gente que conozco, pero nada más. Siento exactamente la misma presión. Quiero ganar un partido más”, asegura Pascual tratando de restar peso a un duelo emotivo. También para Toko Shengelia, que recaló con él en Dubai. “Siempre ha sido especial jugar contra el Barça y siempre lo será”, afirma el georgiano. En un intercambio de banquillos, Pascual se cruzó con Aleksander Sekulic, que cambió Dubai por Barcelona. “Los dos entrenadores conocemos a algún jugador un poquito más en profundidad, pero creo que probablemente mi colega conoce más jugadores que yo”, opina haciendo referencia a la gran renovación sufrida por el equipo azulgrana, que venció en la primera jornada al Efes. Y precisamente el conjunto turco será el rival del Madrid. Al frente, Pablo Laso, que este verano tuvo un pie fuera, aunque finalmente se decidiera su continuidad. El entrenador vitoriano fue protagonista en la segunda edad dorada del baloncesto blanco, lo que se conoció como 'Lasismo'. Desde su llegada en 2011 a su salida en 2022, 22 títulos, incluidas dos Euroligas, seis ACB y otras tantas Copas del Rey. Han pasado cuatro años desde su polémico despido después de sufrir un problema cardíaco y ya se ha enfrentado al Madrid con el Bayern, con el Baskonia y, desde 2025, con el Efes. Los duelos, sin embargo, siguen siendo especiales. “Sigue contando con algunos de los nombres más reconocidos de la Euroliga. Tavares es muy dominante, Campazzo dirige, Maledon es una opción importante, ficharon a Luwawu-Cabarrot y Jantunen... y siempre tienen a Llull”, analiza Laso. Para Pedro Martínez será “un partido muy difícil, aunque en la Euroliga todos lo son. El Efes es un equipo con un talento tremendo que juega a un ritmo muy rápido”. Los dos equipos, además, vienen de perder en la primera jornada: los blancos, en Dubai, y el Efes, en el Palau. Caminos cruzados y enemigos íntimos.

articles.body: El FC Barcelona afronta su primer desplazamiento europeo de la temporada rindiendo visita al Dubái Basketball tras dejar atrás los altibajos del arranque de curso. Los azulgranas, golpeados inicialmente por la derrota en la final de la Supercopa Endesa frente al Joventut, han reaccionado con firmeza encadenando dos triunfos cruciales en el Palau Blaugrana: una sólida victoria continental en el estreno de Euroliga ante el Anadolu Efes (89-82) propulsada por Darío Brizuela y Kevin Punter, y un trabajado triunfo doméstico en la Liga Endesa frente al Leyma Basquet Coruña. Por su parte, el ambicioso proyecto del Dubái Basketball recibe al cuadro catalán en un duelo cargado de incentivos y reencuentros. Liderados desde el banquillo por Xavi Pascual y con Toko Shengelia como referente sobre la pista, el conjunto emiratí busca dar un golpe de autoridad en la máxima competición continental imponiendo su poderío físico en casa. El Barça, revitalizado por la aportación de sus jóvenes y la efectividad de sus hombres exteriores, intentará prolongar su dinámica positiva en una de las canchas más exigentes del calendario europeo. El partido entre el Dubái Basketball y el FC Barcelona, correspondiente a la fase regular de la Euroliga de baloncesto, se disputará este miércoles a partir de las 18:00 horas (horario peninsular español). articles.body: El Real Madrid afronta en Estambul una exigente salida continental en la Euroliga midiéndose al Anadolu Efes en un duelo de reencontrase con aroma a leyenda. El conjunto blanco se verá las caras con Pablo Laso, el técnico que dirigió la segunda edad dorada del club en la última década, en un choque al que los madridistas llegan con la necesidad de estrenar su casillero de victorias europeas tras tropezar ante el Dubái Basketball. La principal novedad en la expedición dirigida por Pedro Martínez es el alta en la competición de Nick Smith Jr., que superadas sus molestias físicas podría debutar y aportar su brillante capacidad anotadora en un perímetro blanco liderado por Facundo Campazzo, Theo Maledon y Timothée Luwawu-Cabarrot. Por su parte, el Anadolu Efes busca hacer valer el factor cancha para sumar su primer triunfo de la temporada continental tras caer ajustadamente frente al Barcelona en la primera jornada. La escuadra otomana, comandada desde el banquillo por Laso, pretende imprimir un ritmo muy elevado al encuentro apoyándose en la anotación de sus figuras exteriores. Ambos equipos acuden a la cita con la intención de quitarse el mal sabor de boca de sus respectivos estrenos y dar un paso al frente en el inicio de esta exigente primera semana con doble compromiso europeo. articles.body: El Valencia Basket afronta este compromiso de la Euroliga con la intención de refrendar las buenas sensaciones continentales mostradas en su estreno ante el Besiktas. El conjunto 'taronja', dirigido desde el banquillo por Xavi Albert, quiere apoyarse en el liderazgo ofensivo de TJ Shorts y la experiencia de Nikola Mirotic para imponer su ritmo de juego sobre la pista. Tras encajar un tropiezo doméstico en el Roig Arena frente al iLerna Lleida, los valencianos buscarán mostrar una versión mucho más sólida en defensa para amarrar la victoria ante su afición en este inicio de competición internacional. Por su parte, el Kosner Baskonia llega a la cita con la urgencia de enderezar su rumbo en el torneo europeo tras caer de forma contundente en el Buesa Arena frente al Olympiacos. La escuadra vitoriana afronta este desplazamiento habiendo sumado un balsámico e agónico triunfo en la Liga Endesa ante el San Pablo Burgos, impulsado por las actuaciones decisivas de AJ Lawson y Chris Duarte en el tramo final. Sin margen para las dudas, el equipo vitoriano intentará ajustar su balance defensivo y explotar el acierto exterior de Markus Howard para asaltar el feudo 'taronja'. El partido entre el Valencia Basket y el Kosner Baskonia, correspondiente a la jornada 2 de la Euroliga de baloncesto, se disputará este martes 29 de septiembre a partir de las 20:30 horas (horario peninsular español). articles.title: Plantón de peso en la NBA: 287 millones en juego y aversión a la báscula
articles.standfirst: Jalen Duren no se ha presentado al media day ni a la pretemporada de los Detroit Pistons tras rechazar una oferta de renovación
articles.summary: Jalen Duren no se ha presentado al media day ni a la pretemporada de los Detroit Pistons tras rechazar una oferta de renovación
articles.body: Jalen Duren, el primer jugador en la NBA nacido después del debut de LeBron James, no se presentó al 'media day' ni al inicio de la pretemporada de los Detroit Pistons por una disputa contractual. El pívot de 22 años y 2,08 m. y 113 kg., que fue el número 13 del Draft de 2022, es agente libre restringido tiene hasta el jueves 1 de octubre para firmar una oferta cualificada de un año y 9,6 millones de dólares o llegar a un acuerdo multianual con la franquicia de Michigan (podría optar a un contrato máximo de 287 millones por cinco años). Según la normativa de la NBA Duren tiene prohibido participar en actividades del equipo hasta que firme un contrato. Los Pistons le ofrecieron a Duren una extensión de contrato totalmente garantizada por 5 años y 200 millones de dólares, la cual sus agentes rechazaron argumentado su preocupación por las cláusulas de peso incluidas en ofertas contractuales anteriores, en los que se exigían controles de peso mensuales para proteger a jugadores de lesiones. La directiva de los Pistons introdujo estas exigencias al considerar de forma interna que el peso de Duren afectó negativamente a su movilidad y rendimiento en los pasados playoffs, en los que bajó sus números a 10,5 puntos, 8,5 rebotes, 2,1 asitencias y 1,1 tapones. "Como saben, hasta ahora no hemos llegado a un acuerdo con Duren. Tiene hasta el jueves para tomar una decisión y estaremos encantados de contar con él, independientemente de la decisión que tome. Fue una pieza clave de nuestro éxito en las dos últimas temporadas. También tuvo una campaña individual extraordinaria el año pasado. Creemos que hará lo mismo en la próxima temporada y estamos entusiasmados por tenerlo de vuelta cuando regrese. Lo integraremos al equipo y tendrá una temporada fantástica, sea cual sea su decisión. Esperamos con interés su regreso", declaró Trajan Langdon, presidente de operaciones de los Pistons. Langdon descartó que Detroit esté explorando opciones de 'sign-and-trade' (firmar y traspasar) y esperan que Duren juegue para Detroit la próxima temporada, ya sea con un contrato a corto o a largo plazo: "Independientemente de cuál sea su decisión, lo que sí podemos controlar es cómo le damos la bienvenida cuando la tome. Será una parte fundamental del equipo, tome la decisión que tome. Será un jugador de los Detroit Pistons y haremos todo lo posible por apoyarlo y sacar su mejor versión, tal como hemos hecho en los últimos dos años; eso no cambiará. Son aspectos que sí podemos controlar. La decisión es, ante todo, algo que podemos controlar". Durante la temporada regular Jalen Duren fue incluido en el tercer mejor quinteto de la NBA tras promediar 19,5 puntos, 10,5 rebotes, 2,0 asistencias y 0,8 tapones por partido, con un 65,0 % de acierto en el tiro en 28,2 minutos de juego.

articles.title: "Hard to fall asleep": Spurs' Victor Wembanyama unveils lasting effects of NBA Finals to Knicks
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs had a lot to say after processing their loss to the Knicks at NBA Media Day.
articles.body:
Coming so close to the Larry O'Brien Trophy but losing has major effects on a team. The San Antonio Spurs had all offseason to process the grief of losing to the New York Knicks . On NBA Media Day, they let their emotions out and revealed how they dealt with such a tough experience. Victor Wembanyama may have had one of the worst things happen to him, which could prompt an even bigger burden to prove himself for the 2026-27 season.

Victor Wembanyama reveals he and Spurs lost sleep after NBA Finals defeat to Knicks

The Spurs have all that it takes to get back up on their feet to once again become NBA title contenders. Coach Mitch Johnson has the luxury of a young core that features Victor Wembanyama, Dylan Harper , Devin Vassell , and Stephon Castle . Adding in a veteran like Tobias Harris means that they will likely be more stable for the 2026-27 NBA season. A lot of their championship hopes have to start somewhere. For the Spurs, it all revolved around getting over the grief of losing to the Knicks in five games.

Wembanyama seems to be the most affected among all of the Spurs players. Some go to the practice facilities and forget the loss ever happened. This is not the case for the Spurs superstar. In fact, he felt one adverse effect that may have increased the size of the chip on his shoulder. He saw the grief manifest through disruptions in his circadian rhythm, via Jared Weiss of The Athletic.

"It's been hard to fall asleep sometimes. Hard emotions. But there is a point where you accept that you have to go through it. You have to feel it all. We don't want to hide from anything," Wembanyama declared on Spurs Media Day.

Everything was going the Spurs' way during the 2025-26 NBA season. They jumped up to 62 wins and got the second seed in the Western Conference. Their hardest matchup was the 64-win Oklahoma City Thunder led by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander . By the Western Conference Finals, any worry about Coach Johnson's schemes and choices was thrown out the window. It was because they beat the best team in the NBA in a seven-game series. Then, all hell broke loose.

The Knicks battered them in Game 1 with a 10-point margin (105-95). A lot of hope was in the air for Game 2, but the Spurs still fell short by two points to get the win (105-104). For a moment, Wembanyama and Co. thought the tide was shifting because they won Game 3 (115-11). However, all of those specks of hope withered away in a painful manner. The immaculate tip-in by OG Anunoby had them lose Game 5 (107-106) to go down 3-1. The hole the Spurs were in had grown too deep by then. It all culminated in a 94-90 Game 5 loss as the Spurs saw another team hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy.

The Spurs vow not to let that happen to them again, to themselves and to their fans. If all goes well, it seems like Wembanyama will secure a second NBA DPOY, his first NBA MVP, and NBA Finals MVP. All of that would put him alongside David Robinson and Tim Duncan in the upper echelon of Spurs bigs to have won the Larry O'Brien trophy.

Losing sleep is one thing, but Wembanyama knows better. He will start and end the season in ways that will turn the tide towards the Spurs. For someone who sleeps very early, he surely will not want his circadian rhythm interrupted again.
